# Haliddirāgajātaka (Ja 435)

**ID:** Ja 435
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Haliddirāgajātaka* (Ja 435) is a canonical Pali Jātaka tale belonging to the *Jātaka* collection. In the commentary edited by V. Fausböll, the Buddha delivered the teaching while dwelling at Jetavana regarding a monk tempted by a coarse or plump maiden (*thullakumāripālobhana*), with the full introductory narrative referred to the *Cullanāradajātaka* in the *Terasanipāta* [Fausböll 1883]. The past story recounts a father and son living as hermits in the Himālayas; when a woman attempts to seduce the son and draw him to the city, his father admonishes him with verses on exercising discrimination in companionship and avoiding uncommitted associations [Anandajoti 2010]. In the concluding identification (*samodhāna*), the son is identified as the discontented monk, the woman as the maiden, and the father as the Buddha himself [Fausböll 1883].

The Pali text was edited in Roman characters by V. Fausböll, whose edition notes manuscript variant titles such as *Haliddhirājajātaka* and *Haliddhijātaka* [Fausböll 1883]. A selection of its verses was translated into English by Bhikkhu Ānandajoti in his anthology *Buddhist Wisdom Verses* [Anandajoti 2010].
